newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake to take Q2 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake to take Q2 restructuring charge.

text.p: Chesapeake Corp said Wednesday it would take a special charge in the second quarter to restructure its specialty packaging and merchandising services organization.

As part of the restructuring, the company said it will close its packaging plant in Sandusky, Ohio, and its Color-Box Inc plant in Buffalo, N.Y. The one-time charge relates to the closings, the company added.
A company spokeswoman said the shutdowns will cut the company's 6,000 workforce by about 200.
She declined to elaborate on the charge's dollar amount other than to say the company will report its second-quarter earnings July 22.
She added the second-quarter results will include a gain from the sale of the West Point, Va., mill and four box plants to St. Laurent Paperboard Inc for $500 million in May.
A June 26 First Call consensus estimate of eight brokers put Chesapeake's earnings at $0.29 a share in the second quarter.
Chesapeake said the plant closings are part of its strategy to align production capacities with current demand and anticipated business growth.

The company said it would combine the three companies in its specialty packaging and merchandising service organization -- Chesapeake Display & Packaging Co, Color-Box Inc and Chesapeake Europe SA -- under one name Chesapeake Display & Packaging Co.
Packaging's and merchandising group vice presdent Andrew Kohut will lead the new business unit, the company added.
Chesapeake's stock traded at 34-5/16 Wednesday morning, up 1/16.
